items.prompt: Which gas in the air do living things need to breathe?

options.why: Nitrogen is the most common gas but we do not use it to breathe.

hints: It makes up about one fifth of the air.
items.explanation: Living things need oxygen, which makes up about one fifth of the air.

items.prompt: The air around us is...
hints: Air is not one single gas.
It has nitrogen, oxygen and more.
items.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.

items.prompt: The layer of gases around the Earth is called the ___.
hints: It begins with the letter a.
items.explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the Earth.

items.prompt: Which gas makes up most of the air?

options.why: Oxygen is about one fifth of the air.
There is only a tiny amount.

hints: It is more than half of the air.
It makes up about four fifths.
We do not breathe it for energy.
items.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about four fifths of the air.

items.prompt: Is seawater pure water?

options.why: Clear water can still contain dissolved substances.

options.text: No, it has salt and other substances dissolved in it.

hints: Taste a drop of the sea.
Pure water has only water in it.
items.explanation: Seawater has salt and other substances dissolved in it, so it is not pure.

items.prompt: Which of these is a source of air pollution?
hints: It goes up into the air.
items.explanation: Smoke from factories and vehicles is air pollution.

items.prompt: Which of these is water pollution?
hints: It harms living things in the water.
items.explanation: Rubbish in a river is water pollution because it harms living things.

items.prompt: Which gases are found in the air?

options.why: Water vapour is a gas but liquid water is not.

hints: Air is a mixture of gases.
Two gases make up almost all of it.
Solids and liquids are not gases.
items.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.

items.prompt: Why is most natural water not pure?

options.text: It has air bubbles in it.
options.why: Air bubbles do not make it impure on their own.

options.text: It has other substances dissolved in it.

hints: Rain picks up gases from the air.
Rivers wash minerals out of the rocks.
items.explanation: Natural water, such as rain, river and sea water, always has some substances dissolved in it.

items.prompt: Pollution is caused when...

options.why: Natural events can cause harm, but pollution means added by humans.

options.text: humans add substances that harm the environment

hints: The word pollution is about people's actions.
items.explanation: Pollution is the introduction of substances by humans that harm the environment.

items.prompt: Sort each example into the kind of pollution it causes.

items.text: harmful chemicals buried in the ground

hints: Think about where the harm happens.
items.explanation: Smoke pollutes air, spilled oil and rubbish pollute water, and chemicals and plastic can pollute soil.

items.prompt: Which action helps reduce pollution?
hints: It does not add harmful substances.
items.explanation: Recycling reduces rubbish and helps to protect the environment.

items.prompt: Substances added by humans that harm the environment are called ___.
items.explanation: Pollution is when humans add harmful substances to the environment.

items.prompt: About what fraction of the air is oxygen?
hints: It is not the largest part.
items.explanation: About one fifth of the air is oxygen. Nitrogen is about four fifths.

items.prompt: A town burns a lot of rubbish near homes. What is the likely effect?

options.text: The smoke pollutes the air and may harm people's breathing.

items.explanation: Burning rubbish adds smoke to the air, which can harm breathing.

items.prompt: Why is the atmosphere important for life on Earth?

options.why: The atmosphere does not change the Earth's size.

options.text: It contains the oxygen that animals need to breathe.
It stops the Earth from spinning.
options.why: It has nothing to do with that.

hints: The air is a mixture of gases.
Without it, animals could not survive.
items.explanation: The atmosphere contains oxygen, which animals and many other living things need to breathe.

items.prompt: Can you tell if water is pure just by looking at it?

options.text: Yes, if it is clear it is pure.
No, clear water can still have substances dissolved in it.
Yes, if it is cold it is pure.

items.explanation: Dissolved substances cannot be seen, so clear water might not be pure.

items.prompt: A farmer sprays too many chemicals on his crops and they wash into a stream. What is this an example of?

options.why: The chemicals went into the stream.
It was caused by a human action.

items.explanation: Chemicals washing into a stream are water pollution.

items.prompt: Why might a polluted river contain fewer fish?

options.text: Fish do not like clear water.
Harmful substances can make the water unsuitable for fish to live in.

items.explanation: Pollutants can poison fish or reduce the oxygen in the water, so fewer fish can live there.

items.prompt: Which is the best way to reduce air pollution in a city?

options.text: use public transport and walk or cycle when possible

hints: Choose the answer that gives out fewer pollutants.
items.explanation: Fewer vehicles on the road means less smoke and fewer pollutants in the air.
